stops.note: 'chat, gossip', from the verb crack 'talk loudly'; Robert Burns's Epistle to J. Lapraik (1785) mentions gathering 'to ca' the crack'
Ulster and Irish English used 'crack' for fun and banter; the Gaelic spelling craic, a borrowing back from English, spread from the 1970s

current_meaning: (Irish) fun, lively conversation and a good time
